items.title: Public read-only SessionTransaction.connections for already acquired connections

labels.name: use case
labels.description: not really a feature or a bug; can be support for new DB features or user use cases not anticipated

items.body:
### Describe the use case

There's no public way to see the connections a `SessionTransaction` already holds. `Session.connection()` checks one out when there is none, and `SessionTransaction.is_active` stays True after its connection is invalidated, so the only way to know that the next statement will raise `PendingRollbackError` is to read `_connections`.

Proposed API, a read-only property on both transaction classes:

```python
SessionTransaction.connections -> Sequence[Connection]
AsyncSessionTransaction.connections -> Sequence[AsyncConnection]
```

It returns a snapshot of the connections the transaction holds, one entry per connection, in the order they were acquired. It never checks out a connection and works in any transaction state. A savepoint returns its own connections, a plain subtransaction its parent's.

discussed in #13684

### Databases / Backends / Drivers targeted

any

### Example Use

```python
import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy import orm

engine = sa.create_engine("sqlite://")
session = orm.Session(engine)

session.execute(sa.text("SELECT 1"))
session.connection().invalidate()  # the database dropped the connection

tx = session.get_transaction()
assert tx.is_active

# today: any(conn.invalidated for conn, *_ in tx._connections.values())
if any(conn.invalidated for conn in tx.connections):
    session.rollback()

session.execute(sa.text("SELECT 1"))  # PendingRollbackError without the rollback
```

### Additional context

_No response_

items.body:
### Describe the use case

see https://docs.python.org/3/library/sqlite3.html#sqlite3.Connection.autocommit for the new feature (which was many years in the making)

from discussion at https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/issues/1655 :


1. SQLAlchemy's documentation needs to be updated to reflect that the "correct transaction control" feature can be enabled as of Python 3.12 using a new flag
2. SQLAlchemy needs more tests in its suite to verify the new flag works. I'm not sure if we have tests for the existing recipe though we should. We ideally would have a test suite that is working through savepoint / transactional DDL / isolation scenarios under all three combinations (existing SQLite, sqlite with the custom recipe, sqlite with the "autocommit=False" recipe)
3.  SQLAlchemy should add support for the new flag at the top level, that is, as an engine option. more docs, more tests. eventually (like, when Python 3.11 is EOL and no longer supported - [October 2027](https://devguide.python.org/versions/)), SQLAlchemy itself can change the default to autocommit=False.


as part of this I think it's time to break out sqlite's test suite into individual files, it's still a big `test_sqlite.py` file.  let's break it out, then a new suite for "test_sqlite_transactional_control.py" where we can exercise tests for ALL of savepoint / transctional ddl / isolation etc. with all combinations of SQLite support.

beyond that I think the documentation at https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/sqlite.html needs to be easier to navigate for this topic.  There's four separate sections that refer to this general topic and they should be consolidated under one section.   the pysqlite-specific section should just refer to the top-level section

this is targeted at 2.1 however we can start with the test suite/ doc changes to be targeted at 2.0/2.1 at the same time.

items.body:
### Describe the bug

With the MSSQL dialect, the DBAPI cursors used for the savepoint statements issued by `begin_nested()` (`SAVE TRANSACTION <name>` and `ROLLBACK TRANSACTION <name>`) are never closed. They are released only when the cursor object is garbage collected. Other statements in the same transaction, including the `IF @@TRANCOUNT = 0 BEGIN TRANSACTION` emitted by `MSDialect.do_savepoint`, are closed normally.

This looks like a small leftover from #12798. Since 2.0.44, `mssql+aioodbc` closes result cursors through aioodbc's awaitable close, but the savepoint cursors still fall through to GC. Under asyncio that free (pyodbc `SQLFreeHandle`) then runs on the event-loop thread. The synchronous `mssql+pyodbc` dialect shows the same unclosed cursors.

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.44, 2.0.54, 2.1.3 (all identical)

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

aioodbc 0.5.0 over pyodbc 5.2.0 (also plain pyodbc 5.2.0)

### Database Vendor and Major Version

Microsoft SQL Server (reproducer uses a fake pyodbc connection; no server needed)

### Python Version

3.11.9

### Operating system

Windows 10 and Linux

### To Reproduce

```python
import asyncio
import gc

import aioodbc
import sqlalchemy
from sqlalchemy import text
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool

UNCLOSED = []
CLOSED = []


class FakeCursor:
    """Stands in for a pyodbc cursor; records whether close() was called."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.closed = False
        self.sql = None
        self.description = None
        self.rowcount = -1
        self.arraysize = 1

    def execute(self, sql, *params):
        self.sql = sql
        self.rowcount = 1
        return self

    def fetchall(self):
        return []

    def nextset(self):
        return False

    def setinputsizes(self, *sizes):
        pass

    def close(self):
        self.closed = True
        CLOSED.append(self.sql)

    def __del__(self):
        if not self.closed:
            UNCLOSED.append(self.sql)


class FakePyodbcConnection:
    autocommit = False

    def cursor(self):
        return FakeCursor()

    def commit(self):
        pass

    def rollback(self):
        pass

    def close(self):
        pass

    def add_output_converter(self, *args):
        pass

    def getinfo(self, *args):
        return "16.00.1000"


async def creator():
    conn = aioodbc.Connection(dsn="unused")
    conn._conn = FakePyodbcConnection()  # skip the real ODBC connect
    return conn


def report(label):
    gc.collect()
    print(f"{label}: closed={len(CLOSED)} unclosed={len(UNCLOSED)}")
    for sql in UNCLOSED:
        print(f"    not closed: {sql}")
    CLOSED.clear()
    UNCLOSED.clear()


async def main():
    print("sqlalchemy", sqlalchemy.__version__, "aioodbc", aioodbc.__version__)
    engine = create_async_engine(
        "mssql+aioodbc://", async_creator=creator, poolclass=NullPool, _initialize=False
    )

    async with engine.connect() as conn:
        await conn.begin()
        sp = await conn.begin_nested()
        await conn.execute(text("UPDATE t SET x = 1"))
        await sp.rollback()
        await conn.rollback()
    report("Core begin_nested + rollback")

    async with AsyncSession(engine) as session:
        async with session.begin_nested():
            await session.execute(text("UPDATE t SET x = 1"))
        await session.rollback()
    report("ORM begin_nested + release")

    await engine.dispose()


asyncio.run(main())
```

### Error

No exception; the output shows which cursors were never closed (identical on 2.0.44, 2.0.54 and 2.1.3):

```
sqlalchemy 2.0.44 aioodbc 0.5.0
Core begin_nested + rollback: closed=2 unclosed=2
    not closed: SAVE TRANSACTION sa_savepoint_1
    not closed: ROLLBACK TRANSACTION sa_savepoint_1
ORM begin_nested + release: closed=2 unclosed=1
    not closed: SAVE TRANSACTION sa_savepoint_1
```

The same Core sequence on a synchronous `create_engine("mssql+pyodbc://", creator=..., poolclass=NullPool)` with the same fake connection gives `unclosed ['SAVE TRANSACTION sa_savepoint_1', 'ROLLBACK TRANSACTION sa_savepoint_1']` on 2.0.44 and 2.1.3.

### Additional context

The practical cost is small. Against a real SQL Server (ODBC Driver 17, pyodbc 5.2.0), freeing a cursor for a non-parameterized statement such as `SAVE TRANSACTION` took a median of 0.014 ms (p95 0.031 ms, n=60) and did no network work. By comparison, a parameterized statement's free took about 3.3 ms, because it is a server round trip. So this isn't a performance problem in practice; I'm reporting it because it's the one remaining path where an asyncio application still frees cursors on the event loop by GC after #12798.

items.title: Add Redis ADBC to the external dialects documentation
items.body:
Please add Redis (via ADBC) to the External Dialects table in `doc/build/dialects/index.rst`, linking `adbc-driver-redis` to its [SQLAlchemy setup and limitations](https://github.com/alberttwong/redis-adbc-driver/blob/main/docs/python-integrations.md#sqlalchemy-and-superset).

The [Redis ADBC driver](https://github.com/alberttwong/redis-adbc-driver) includes a SQLAlchemy dialect registered as `redis.adbc` and `rediss.adbc`. It provides PostgreSQL SQL compilation and catalog reflection. It is an autocommit analytics connector; rollback cannot undo writes, and savepoints and two-phase transactions are unsupported.

With the driver wheel and its `sqlalchemy` extra installed, and Redis running locally:

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text

engine = create_engine("redis+adbc://localhost:6379/0")
with engine.connect() as conn:
    print(conn.execute(text("SELECT :value AS value"), {"value": 42}).all())
engine.dispose()
```

The proposed documentation change adds one table row, between OpenGauss and Rockset, and its link target. Following the contribution guidelines, I am opening this issue first to request approval for that documentation PR.

items.title: asyncpg connection returned to pool with open transaction after cancellation inside before_cursor_execute

labels.name: engine
labels.description: engines, connections, transactions, isolation levels, execution options

items.body:
### Describe the bug

 With AsyncEngine + postgresql+asyncpg, I can reproduce a pooled connection being returned to the pool while PostgreSQL still has an open transaction.

 The repro involves a `before_cursor_execute` listener that performs an inner DBAPI-style `cursor.execute(...)` (eg to set a PostgreSQL session RLS). If task cancellation happens while that inner execute triggers asyncpg’s implicit BEGIN, SQLAlchemy can check the connection back into the pool without invalidating/terminating it.

 On later reuse, SQLAlchemy appears to think it is starting a top-level transaction, but asyncpg sees an existing
 `_top_xact` and emits `SAVEPOINT __asyncpg_savepoint_*`. Rollback/commit then only affects the savepoint, leaving the hidden outer transaction open.

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.51

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

asyncpg 0.31.0

### Database Vendor and Major Version

PostgreSQL 18

### Python Version

3.14

### Operating system

Linux, macOS

### To Reproduce

```python
import asyncio
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass

import asyncpg
from sqlalchemy import event, text
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine, AsyncConnection

DEFAULT_URL = "postgresql+asyncpg://localhost/postgres"
INNER_SQL = "SET LOCAL myapp.context = 'x'"


def sqlalchemy_url() -> str:
    url = os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", DEFAULT_URL)
    if url.startswith("postgresql://"):
        return "postgresql+asyncpg://" + url.removeprefix("postgresql://")
    return url


def asyncpg_url(url: str) -> str:
    return url.replace("postgresql+asyncpg://", "postgresql://", 1)


@dataclass
class Snapshot:
    state: str | None
    query: str | None
    xact_start: object


async def pg_stat(url: str, pid: int) -> Snapshot:
    conn = await asyncpg.connect(
        asyncpg_url(url),
        server_settings={"application_name": "sqlalchemy-asyncpg-repro-observer"},
    )
    try:
        row = await conn.fetchrow(
            """
            select state, query, xact_start
            from pg_stat_activity
            where pid = $1
            """,
            pid,
        )
        if row is None:
            return Snapshot(None, None, None)
        return Snapshot(row["state"], row["query"], row["xact_start"])
    finally:
        await conn.close()


def print_activity(label: str, snap: Snapshot) -> None:
    print(f"{label}:")
    print(f"  state: {snap.state}")
    print(f"  query: {snap.query}")
    print(f"  xact_start: {snap.xact_start}")


def _get_server_pid(conn: AsyncConnection):
    return conn.sync_connection.connection.driver_connection.get_server_pid()


async def run_once(attempt: int, max_attempts: int) -> bool:
    url = sqlalchemy_url()
    engine = create_async_engine(url, pool_size=1, max_overflow=0)
    armed = False

    @event.listens_for(engine.sync_engine, "before_cursor_execute")
    def before_cursor_execute(
        conn, cursor, statement, parameters, context, executemany
    ):
        nonlocal armed
        if armed:
            return
        armed = True
        # The inner cursor.execute() will first call SQLAlchemy's asyncpg
        # adapter _start_transaction().  Cancel the current task as soon as
        # control returns to the event loop, i.e. while that implicit BEGIN is
        # in progress.
        task = asyncio.current_task()
        asyncio.get_running_loop().call_soon(task.cancel)
        cursor.execute(INNER_SQL)

    try:
        try:
            async with engine.connect() as conn:
                pid = _get_server_pid(conn)
                await conn.execute(text("select 1"))
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass

        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)

        print(f"server pid: {pid}")
        before = await pg_stat(url, pid)
        print_activity("pg_stat_activity after cancellation", before)

        async with engine.connect() as conn:
            pid = _get_server_pid(conn)

            try:
                async with conn.begin():
                    await conn.execute(text("select 42"))
                    raise RuntimeError("force rollback")
            except RuntimeError:
                pass

            after = await pg_stat(url, pid)
            print_activity("pg_stat_activity after forced rollback", after)
            print(f"xact_start unchanged: {after.xact_start == before.xact_start}")

            return after.xact_start == before.xact_start
    finally:
        event.remove(engine.sync_engine, "before_cursor_execute", before_cursor_execute)
        await engine.dispose()


async def main() -> None:
    max_attempts = int(os.environ.get("REPRO_ATTEMPTS", "5"))
    for attempt in range(1, max_attempts + 1):
        if await run_once(attempt, max_attempts):
            return
    raise SystemExit("race did not reproduce; increase REPRO_ATTEMPTS and retry")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Error

```
server pid: 94801
pg_stat_activity after cancellation:
  state: idle in transaction
  query: BEGIN;
  xact_start: 2026-06-17 08:57:19.372350+00:00
pg_stat_activity after forced rollback:
  state: idle in transaction
  query: ROLLBACK TO __asyncpg_savepoint_6__;
  xact_start: 2026-06-17 08:57:19.372350+00:00
xact_start unchanged: True
```

### Additional context

In real world, it happens at my company when a Websocket client disconnects "at the wrong time".

**Describe your question**

Trying to setup "Joining a Session into an External Transaction (such as for test suite)" recipe for `pytest` and `asyncio` API 

**Example**
sync `pytest` recipe works fine

```Python
import pytest
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from sqlalchemy import event, Column, Integer, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base

Base = declarative_base()

# a model
class Thing(Base):
    __tablename__ = "thing"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def engine_fixture():
    engine = create_engine("postgresql://postgres:changethis@db/app_test", echo=True)
    Base.metadata.drop_all(engine)
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

    yield engine

    Base.metadata.drop_all(engine)


@pytest.fixture
def session(engine_fixture):
    conn = engine_fixture.connect()
    trans = conn.begin()
    session = Session(bind=conn)

    def _fixture(session):
        session.add_all([Thing(), Thing(), Thing()])
        session.commit()

    # load fixture data within the scope of the transaction
    _fixture(session)

    # start the session in a SAVEPOINT...
    session.begin_nested()

    # then each time that SAVEPOINT ends, reopen it
    @event.listens_for(session, "after_transaction_end")
    def restart_savepoint(session, transaction):
        if transaction.nested and not transaction._parent.nested:
            session.begin_nested()

    yield session

    # same teardown from the docs
    session.close()
    trans.rollback()
    conn.close()


def _test_thing(session, extra_rollback=0):

    rows = session.query(Thing).all()
    assert len(rows) == 3

    for elem in range(extra_rollback):
        # run N number of rollbacks
        session.add_all([Thing(), Thing(), Thing()])
        rows = session.query(Thing).all()
        assert len(rows) == 6

        session.rollback()

    # after rollbacks, still @ 3 rows
    rows = session.query(Thing).all()
    assert len(rows) == 3

    session.add_all([Thing(), Thing()])
    session.commit()

    rows = session.query(Thing).all()
    assert len(rows) == 5

    session.add(Thing())
    rows = session.query(Thing).all()
    assert len(rows) == 6

    for elem in range(extra_rollback):
        # run N number of rollbacks
        session.add_all([Thing(), Thing(), Thing()])
        rows = session.query(Thing).all()
        if elem > 0:
            # b.c. we rolled back that other "thing" too
            assert len(rows) == 8
        else:
            assert len(rows) == 9
        session.rollback()

    rows = session.query(Thing).all()
    if extra_rollback:
        assert len(rows) == 5
    else:
        assert len(rows) == 6


def test_thing_one_pytest(session):
    # run zero rollbacks
    _test_thing(session, 0)


def test_thing_two_pytest(session):
    # run two extra rollbacks
    _test_thing(session, 2)
```

port to `asyncio` API, togheter with `pytest-asyncio` (0.14.0) fails, due to wrong/malfunctioning `teardown` of the first test-case:

```Python
E       assert 8 == 3
E         +8
E         -3

test_async.py:75: AssertionError
```

Any clues on what I could be doing wrong? Worth mentioning is that `restart_savepoint` is forced to use `AsyncSession.sync_session` for listeners, as async listeners are not yet implemented, could it be a reason?

 - Python: Python 3.8.5
 - SQLAlchemy: 1.4@b1
 - Database: postgres:12
 - pytest: 6.1.2
 - pytest-asyncio: 0.14.0
 - DBAPI: asyncpg 0.21.0

Thanks!

items.title: Explicit commit in transaction context manager causes error.

labels.name: engine
labels.description: engines, connections, transactions, isolation levels, execution options

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

when explicitly committing a transaction in a context manager, it throws an error, this seems to be caused by a `_assert_active` call in `Transaction.__exit__`.

this is implied to work via code examples in the docs and it looks like the code following the assert handles a a transaction being already committed and just returns early?

**Expected behavior**
No error

**To Reproduce**

```py
import sqlalchemy.orm

engine = sqlalchemy.create_engine(
    "postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/postgres", 
    future=True,
)

with sqlalchemy.orm.Session(engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:
    with session.begin():
        session.execute("SELECT 1")
        session.commit()
```

**Error**

```pytb
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "{snip}/test.py", line 10, in <module>
    session.commit()
  File "{snip}/lib/python3.9/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/session.py", line 937, in __exit__
    self._assert_active(deactive_ok=True, prepared_ok=True)
  File "{snip}/lib/python3.9/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/session.py", line 617, in _assert_active
    raise sa_exc.ResourceClosedError(closed_msg)
sqlalchemy.exc.ResourceClosedError: This transaction is closed
```

**Versions.**
 - OS: linux
 - Python: 3.9
 - SQLAlchemy: 1.4.8
 - Database: postgres
 - DBAPI: psycopg2 or asyncpg
